title: Seamless major-version transition playbook and customer comms kit
creator: Asha Raman
description: Create a complete, customer-facing playbook and asset kit to support a major runtime version transition (2.0) that introduces LTS and rolling channels, refined rollout gates, and automated SDK upgrade tooling. The kit should make upgrades low-friction for self-serve customers while providing clear escalation paths for enterprise customers. Deliverables must include a human-readable changelog template emphasizing compatibility changes, an interactive compatibility matrix, templated emails and in-app banner content, SDK migration snippets, a staged rollback notice, and a short FAQ for common breaking-change scenarios.
acceptance_criteria: Changelog template and single-page migration summary available in Drive and Confluence
Compatibility matrix covers API surface, model variants, and quantization/kv-cache implications
Three templated email variants produced: opt-in alpha, recommended upgrade, enterprise SLA notice
In-app banner copy and one-line notification for Console release flow reviewed by Design
SDK snippets for Python and JavaScript validated against runtime-2.0-beta and published to SDK repo
Rollout gate triggers documented and mapped to Console flags with clear customer-facing wording
Stakeholder sign-off from Support, Sales, Eng (runtime), and Security
deliverables: Drive: 2.0 Major Version Migration Guide (customer-facing) - link to draft
Confluence: Internal playbook for Support + Sales escalation paths
Release notes template: summary + compatibility section + migration steps
Compatibility matrix CSV and interactive view (hosted on docs.redwood)
Email templates (opt-in, recommended, enterprise) + translation keys
Console banner and modal copy + assets for in-product migration prompt
SDK upgrade snippets and PRs in github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python and sdk-js
Rollback notice template and automated rollback checklist for SREs

notes: Trade-offs discussed: aggressive deprecation schedule keeps runtime clean but increases short-term support load; decided on 6-month deprecation window for non-critical legacy headers and 12-month for major semantic changes.
Decision log: use "opt-in" channel labeling for early adopters and a staged 'recommended' push for the majority. Enterprises get a dedicated migration window and a rollback SLA in contract addenda.
Open questions: do we provide automatic rewriters in the SDK for the kv-cache header rename? Eng estimates impact at 4 story points across two SDKs.
Risks: Customers using custom routing/pinning may experience transient errors during canary gates; include explicit checklist items for them and contact points for Solutions Engineering.
Communication cadence: public release notes + in-product banner on release day, follow-up email 72 hours later with personalized guidance based on usage patterns.
